newsitem.title: USA: Florida consumer confidence hits eight-year high.
newsitem.headline: Florida consumer confidence hits eight-year high.

text.p: Florida's consumer confidence index hit an eight-year high in June, but retail sales are reaching a saturation point, University of Florida economists said Tuesday.

The index gained three points in June, rising to 100 on a combination of healthy wages and low unemployment. The last time the index was that high was in June 1989, when it hit 101 a year before the start of the last recession.

"Consumer confidence both here in Florida and nationally is through the roof," said Survey Director Chris McCarty. "This is an unusual set of circumstances. While wages are up, unemployment, interest rates and inflation are low. Yet the demand for goods has not outpaced the supply, despite what should be a consumer sector flush with money."
Auto and home sales have begun to drop and retail sales have slackened in Florida and nationally, the survey found.
"The decline may be the natural result of consumers reaching a point where they have already made most of their major purchases," McCarty said.
The softening in sales may also reflect a less aggressive approach by credit card companies in offering credit, UF economist Dave Denslow said.
Perceptions that this is a good time to buy a house fell two points in June.

Respondents gave mixed reports of business activity. Fifty-three percent said business was better than a year ago, the same percentage as in May. But the share who said the expected additional employees to be hired at their workplace in the next six months fell to 35 percent in June from 40 percent in May.
The monthly survey was based on telephone interviews with 824 randomly selected Florida adults and has a three perent error margin.
